title: Alaska Picks Its Youngest Governor Ever
summary:
Alaska has a new governor: Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, 37, the youngest governor in Alaska's history.

Kreiss-Tomkins used to be a state representative from Sitka, a small island town. People call him JKT. He wants to work with Democrats, Republicans, and independents, and called himself a "man of the middle" at a debate.

Many leaders backed him: three former governors, a Democrat, a Republican, and an independent, plus Senator Lisa Murkowski. "I strongly believe people just want things to work, and want people to work together," he said.

It took more than a week to count the votes, including mail votes and votes from far-away parts of the state. Alaska uses ranked-choice voting, where voters rank candidates in order. Kreiss-Tomkins beat three Republicans, and a winner needs more than half the votes.

Voters also voted on whether to end ranked-choice voting. That idea failed, so the system will stay.

Kreiss-Tomkins starts work at noon on December 7. He will lead a state where many people say things are not working well, costs are rising, and schools have closed.
